"Worse" is pretty subjective, and it seems like people are exposed to a variety of 'personal hells' when communicating with this SCP. Plus we don't know what happens (mentally) to the people who don't disappear; are they subjected to the images/sensations of the torture they would have experienced?

Also, for all of SCPs I would consider "worse", trauma would be the least concerning outcome.

item.title: Re: Another clarification needed:
item.content:encoded:
That still doesn't make her "stupid".

• The phone may be her only hope at contacting the outside world; you don't know what's on the other side.

• She probably doesn't know/remember how she got there or any of the other details. Or she might be giving them that information in her attempts to plead for help; we weren't given the full details of what she's saying.

They do say they attempt to track the call and it isn't possible.

I'm going to go ahead and NOT ASSUME that she's stupid. If she would deliberately minimize her chances of survival, yeah she'd be stupid. But there's a lot of mystery to this article, and it's a very strange to assume without sufficient evidence that someone is purposely withholding information that may free them from something like this.

I always quite liked this one, it has lost a but of its lustre as its aged. The central idea is intriguing, but is pulled off in quite a coarse fashion. I would love to see this reworked.

Regardless, I have an issue with the following sentence.

Depending on the level of trauma of affected personnel, they may be required to submit to consultation with an approved psychiatrist for no less than two weeks.

First, there's almost no explicit justification for taking this action. Researchers are exposed to worse things at the foundation, without having to include this in containment procedures. But more importantly - why a psychiatrist specifically? Unless medication was required, a psychologist would be the correct choice for this situation.

item.title: Image Team

I've done a reverse image search and couldn't find anything substantial. In cases like these I suggest the image be left up until we're contacted regarding its use. We do this with the assumption that contact would be highly unlikely. I don't think the take down was warranted and I recommend against this sort of action until there's been a dialogue in its regard.

That being said, the image is horrible and I wouldn't be sad to see it replaced.

item.title: Re: Another clarification needed:
item.content:encoded:
Getting rid of 682 by handing it over to the custody of malevolent abductor entities has been tried a whole bunch of times already, both in tales and the test logs. The best case scenario is invariably that they give it back, and the worst case scenario is that they give it back at an unspecified place and time.
